question: {If } tantheta + cottheta = 4, { then } sec²theta times csc²theta { is equal to:}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: (tanθ + cotθ)² = tan²θ + cot²θ + 2

4² = tan²θ + cot²θ + 2 ⇒ tan²θ + cot²θ = 14

sec²θ × csc²θ = (1 + tan²θ)(1 + cot²θ)

= 1 + tan²θ + cot²θ + 1 = 16

**∴ Answer = 16**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tanθ + cotθ = 4

**Formula used:**

sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ and csc²θ = 1 + cot²θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ (tanθ + cotθ)² = tan²θ + cot²θ + 2

⇒ 16 = tan²θ + cot²θ + 2

⇒ tan²θ + cot²θ = 14

⇒ sec²θ × csc²θ = (1 + tan²θ)(1 + cot²θ)

⇒ = 1 + tan²θ + cot²θ + tan²θ·cot²θ

⇒ Since tanθ·cotθ = 1 ⇒ tan²θ·cot²θ = 1

⇒ = 1 + 14 + 1 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identity

sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ, csc²θ = 1 + cot²θ

Key Relation

tanθ × cotθ = 1

Square Identity

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab
